newsitem.title: INDIA: India urges state to help in wheat procurement.
newsitem.headline: India urges state to help in wheat procurement.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Saturday urged the chief minister of the agriculturally-rich Punjab province to "cooperate" in wheat procurement, a government spokesman said.
The spokesman said Deve Gowda met Prakash Singh Badal and asked to take a "pragmatic approach" on the issue.

Newspapers reported that Badal, who heads a government formed by a Sikh party with a strong following among farmers, had threatened to curb procurement if the government did not raise prices to 5.25 rupees from 4.15 rupees per kg.
Deve Gowda told Badal that the likely financial burden on the government and the interests of both farmers and consumers had to be kept in mind while deciding on wheat procurement prices.
The government buys wheat to build up its buffer stocks, which it then uses to control prices by releasing stocks through a state-run distribution system.
